components.institution_label: Parental Leaves of Absence With Modified Duties
components.description: Policy 6-315 disability leave for an eligible faculty member who gives birth: a parental leave of absence with modified duties for one semester (or equivalent period for twelve-month faculty), released from professional duties, at 95% of annual base salary.
components.mechanism_note: A leave of absence the University pays at 95% of base salary under its own parental-leave policy; the 'modified duties' are a release from professional duties, so it is coded as a paid leave, not as modified duties on active service.
components.faculty_group_note: Policy 6-315: 'academic librarians and regular faculty in all colleges except the School of Medicine'; 'Regular faculty' is defined as tenured or tenure-eligible faculty under Policy 6-300; eligible faculty have appointments that began before the expected arrival of a child
components.faculty_scope: all colleges except the School of Medicine
components.eligible_parent_wording: an eligible faculty member who gives birth to a child; 'disability leaves for birth mothers'
components.service_requirement: appointment began before the expected arrival of the child
components.dual_employee_rule: Only one University of Utah faculty member is guaranteed to qualify for parental benefits for a given instance of childbirth or adoption
components.entitlement_note: 'will be granted' upon approval of a request, and the eligible member 'is guaranteed parental benefits' (up to twice): the approval covers the arrangements (V2; schema: shall be granted upon request).
components.duration_note: One semester for faculty on nine-month appointments, or an equivalent period for faculty on twelve-month appointments; the disability leave ends 'at the end of the semester (or 12-week period) for which the leave is sought'.
components.pay_note: A department or college may supplement above 95%, applied consistently within the unit; grant-funded portions follow actual effort.
components.relief_note: 'released from professional duties during this period'; the member may choose to continue some activities (meeting students, research, hiring or RPT decisions). The member 'should generally teach one-half of a normal load, overall for an academic year'.
components.time_window: birth during the semester for which leave is sought or within four weeks before it; leave begins no more than three months before the birth and ends at the end of the semester (or 12-week period)
components.use_limit_note: 'An eligible faculty member is guaranteed parental benefits no more than twice.' Later requests for further births or adoptions are subject to the senior vice president's approval. 'Parental benefits' covers both the leave and the review extension.
components.notice: should normally be requested no fewer than three months before the expected arrival of the child (on the Parental Benefits application form)
components.return_obligation: Policy 6-314 Section 9.B applies: return to University service for at least the length of the leave, or a proportionate refund of compensation (waivable for extreme hardship)

notes: Governing faculty documents are saved: Policy 6-315 (Faculty Parental Benefits, Rev. 2, eff. 2011-07-01) covers regular (tenured and tenure-eligible) faculty and academic librarians in all colleges except the School of Medicine, so missing is false. The School of Medicine policy (Policy 8-002) is not saved and not coded.

2018_07 (faculty handbook page) is a link index with no policy text. 2018_01 (examples) states it is not part of the policy; it adds no provision. 2018_06 (application form, file dated 12-2013, capture 2015) is consistent with 6-315 (95% salary, concurrent FMLA, obligation to return 'for at least one semester') but says the leave request 'must be made within three months after arrival of the child', whereas 6-315 says it 'should normally be made no fewer than three months prior'; the policy's notice is coded. The form is not cited as evidence.

Calendar: semesters (6-315 'one semester for faculty in nine-month appointments'; 6-314 sabbaticals of 'one or two semesters'); no length stated, so calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order. 6-315's academic year (Aug 16-May 15) is a definition, not a term length.

The 6-315 leave is one semester per birth, taken as the disability leave (birth mother) or the care-giving leave (majority caregiver); coded as two components linked in_lieu_of. Twelve-month faculty get 'an equivalent period' (the disability leave ends at the end of the 'semester (or 12-week period)').

Birth parent chain: disability leave with modified duties, 1 semester at 95% (c1), with FMLA 12 workweeks running from its start (c3, concurrent); or the care-giving leave (c2) in lieu of c1. For her own serious health condition: sick-leave balance (c10, concurrent with FMLA) -> Extended Sick Leave up to 30 days (c11, discretionary, after balances) ; unpaid medical leave with reinstatement (c12, discretionary) after FMLA, within the 26-week own-health limit.

Non-birth parent chain: care-giving leave, 1 semester at 95% if the majority caregiver (c2), with FMLA 12 workweeks concurrent from its start (c3). Only one University faculty member is guaranteed parental benefits per birth.
Policy 6-311 tenure-clock clauses (c6-c9) are coded beside the 6-315 review extension (c4, c5); 6-315 says it governs where inconsistent.

Not components: sabbatical, administrative and librarian academic leaves (6-314 ss. 4-8: professional-improvement purposes only); Option B medical leave without reinstatement (separation with benefits extension; not job-protected); ADA reasonable accommodation (disability accommodation); sick-to-vacation conversion (excludes faculty).

Cross-references not saved: Policy 8-002 (SOM parental leave); Policy 5-201 (non-health leaves, incl. special personal reasons); Policy 5-301 (Vacation); Policy 5-117 (ADA); Policy 5-303 (insurance programs, LTD); Policy 6-320 (partial leaves below .75 FTE); Procedure 5-200A; Rule 5-200B (UUHC staff only); Policy 5-001; Policy 5-202; Policy 5-403; Policy 6-300; Policy 6-302; Policy 6-303; Policy 6-309; Policy 6-313; Policy 6-319; Policy 2-005; Policy 1-001/Rule 1-001; 29 CFR 825.100 et seq.; Parental Leave Policy Evaluation (Utah Educational Policy Center 2010).
